title: Singular personal partitive pronouns
summary: Use minua, sinua or häntä when a verb takes a singular partitive object: Odotan häntä. — I am waiting for her.
objectives: Use minua, sinua and häntä for a singular personal object.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Use minua, sinua and häntä for a singular personal object.
A personal object pronoun refers to the person the action concerns. The person doing the action can be different. The dictionary forms minä, sinä and hän are not these object forms.
Learn minä → minua (I → me), sinä → sinua (you → you, one person), and hän → häntä (he or she → him or her). Finnish häntä does not specify gender.
keyPoints: Use minua, sinua or häntä as the singular personal object in this taught verb pattern.

steps: Use minua, sinua or häntä as the singular personal object in this taught verb pattern.
Odotat means “you are waiting for” and works as the verb. odotat comes from odottaa: odota- + -t, with tt → t.
minua means “me” and works as the partitive pronoun used as the object of the action. The standard written partitive form of minä is minua; learn this pronoun form directly.
Use minua, sinua or häntä as the singular personal object in this taught verb pattern.
Autan means “I help” and works as the verb. autan comes from auttaa: auta- + -n, with tt → t.
sinua means “you, one person” and works as the partitive pronoun used as the object of the action. The standard written partitive form of sinä is sinua; learn this pronoun form directly.
Use minua, sinua or häntä as the singular personal object in this taught verb pattern.
Odotan means “I am waiting for” and works as the verb. odotan comes from odottaa: odota- + -n, with tt → t.
häntä means “him or her” and works as the partitive pronoun used as the object of the action. The standard written partitive form of hän is häntä; learn this pronoun form directly.
Use minua, sinua or häntä as the singular personal object in this taught verb pattern.
Kuuntelen means “I am listening to” and works as the verb. kuuntelen comes from kuunnella: kuuntele- + -n, with nn → nt and the e stem.
sinua means “you, one person” and works as the partitive pronoun used as the object of the action. The standard written partitive form of sinä is sinua; learn this pronoun form directly.

commonMistakes: Do not use the subject form for this partitive object.
Häntä can refer to a man or a woman.
The spoken shortened forms are outside this standard-written lesson.
